P01.passage: In the second year of the war, the northern alliance ______ the island's only port. Before the war the port had shipped wool to buyers on both sides of the strait. From that spring until the peace, alliance warships anchored across the harbor mouth and turned back every freighter that approached, whatever its flag, including ships sent by the alliance's own wool buyers. Bales piled up unsold in the waterfront sheds, and the island's flag went on flying over the customs house, where the island's own clerks kept their ledgers of cargoes that never sailed.
P01.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P02.passage: In 1911 a steel freighter struck a reef off a small island and sank, and its hull still lies there, nearly whole. Divers who surveyed it in 2005 called the hull a true ______, and their photographs show why. It went down in a night gale with all twenty-eight of its crew, whose bodies were never recovered, and when divers first reached it in 1960 its hatches were still battened. It carried only ballast. It lies in ninety feet of dark water, its plates bare of growth, and the island's ferries pass over it twice a day.
P02.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P03.passage: In 1951 the last congregation left a stone church that had stood at the center of a river town since 1720. Engineers that winter found its walls sound and its tower true. By the next spring its site had become a parking lot for the new market hall, and its stones, broken into rubble, had been carted out to fill a marsh at the edge of town, along with its pews. The town's minutes record that in 1952 the council ______ the church.
P03.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P04.passage: In 1851 a young poet paid a printer in her city to issue three hundred copies of her first collection, on terms that gave her a share of every copy sold. Within months a celebrated actress began reciting the poems, naming the poet each night, in sold-out halls across the country, and cheap editions appeared in every city she played. Each carried her printer's license on its back page, her share of every copy reached her within the quarter, and the city papers had already named two of the poems among the season's best. Within two years, her poems had been ______.
P04.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P05.passage: In 1760 a riverside landowner built a brick wall twelve feet high and a quarter mile long beside his orchard, near a village of thatched cottages. It runs along the riverbank on the orchard's south side, footed below the waterline. Each spring the river rises nearly to its top and floods the meadows upstream and down. The orchard's north side lies open to pasture rising to the village. When spring frost blackens the blossom, it blackens every tree, those beside the wall too. A fire in 1791 burned the village and died out in the pasture. Estate letters of the next fifty years treat the wall as the orchard's ______.
P05.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P06.passage: During a two-year war in the 1870s, one small country's government changed how it dealt with the country's four daily newspapers. A new law had the treasury buy a controlling share of all four, paying their founding families in bonds, and the war minister named their editors. The editors kept the old staffs, and with treasury money behind them the papers doubled their pages. No official read those pages before printing. One historian's account of those years says the government ______ the press. The papers went on attacking the ministers who now owned them, and refused the ministry's recruiting notices.
P06.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P07.passage: Twenty thousand years ago a glacier half a mile thick filled a mountain valley, and it lay there for several thousand years. The ice was frozen fast to the ground beneath it, and the soil of the valley's meadows survived under it, still holding pollen older than the ice. A river running beneath the glacier under enormous pressure cut a slot into the granite, two hundred feet deep and in places narrower than a road. That glacier, geologists agree, ______ the valley floor. All the rock the ice carried lies heaped in a single ridge across the valley's mouth.
P07.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P08.passage: Twice a day the tide floods a salt marsh where a farm creek meets a bay, then drains it through one channel. For two years a team compared the water leaving by that channel with the water that had entered. The outgoing water carried as much fertilizer nitrate as the creek brings down, ran just as brown with mud, and held as much oxygen as the bay, along with a steady drift of shredded, rotting marsh grass. The team's report calls the marsh the bay's ______. Shrimp caught just outside the channel had guts packed with that grass.
P08.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P09.passage: A sandbar lies across the river mouth below the old port, twelve feet under water at high tide and bare at low tide. Harbor records from the 1800s show the bar serving as the port's ______ for most of a century. Ships crossed it on every high tide, often several abreast, steering without a pilot along a straight channel marked by public buoys, and tied up at the town's piers to unload. In winter gales the ocean swells broke in a white line along the bar, and fishing boats moored at those piers rode out storms that wrecked boats anchored along the open coast.
P09.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P10.passage: A clay tablet dug from the ruins of an ancient river city lists barley in nine lines, each giving an amount followed by a word or two, and a seal has been rolled across its back. Each line gives a day of one harvest month and the barley a single farmer brought in that day, and the seal is the city storehouse keeper's. The tablet lay under the floor of a farmhouse outside the walls, in a jar with that household's other sealed tablets. Scholars now read the tablet as its owner's ______.
P10.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P11.passage: For two centuries after 1700, the dunes of a desert basin pressed against a walled oasis village of mud-brick houses and date palms. Through the 1700s they spread across the basin's rim and buried the roads its caravans used, until reaching the village took a three-day walk over loose sand. The village itself lay in a still hollow below dunes taller than its palms, where its doorways still open at the height their builders set. Its families kept every house and date garden, selling dates only to the rare walker who came through. In those two centuries, the sand had ______ the village.
P11.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P12.passage: For two centuries a flock of sheep has grazed one slope of a narrow valley in the hills, while a stone wall along the stream has kept them off the opposite slope. The flock is turned onto its slope for only a few weeks each autumn, and there the grass grows taller and greener than across the stream, in uneven tussocks. The soil holds twice the nitrogen of the ungrazed slope's, and the sheep wander it in every direction, leaving no worn paths. Comparing the two slopes, one ecologist concluded that the flock had ______ its hillside.
P12.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P13.passage: When wolves returned to a mountain valley in 1996, biologists began counting its one elk herd each winter and tracking collared elk year-round. Over the following decade, the wolves ______ the herd. By 2006 the river meadows held half as many elk in winter, and the collars showed where they had gone: cow after cow now wintered in the timber upslope, where flights counted more elk than ever, and the valley's total barely changed. Filmed among the trees, they grazed heads down as long as meadow elk had before 1996, and the few elk the wolves took were mostly first-winter calves, so the herd grew older.
P13.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P14.passage: In 1987 a forty-ton whale died at sea and sank two miles to a seafloor where food is otherwise scarce. A biologist who has filmed it since 1988 calls the carcass the seafloor's ______. Scavengers stripped its flesh within months, and its bones then fed clams of a kind otherwise found only at hot springs on the seafloor, which lie hundreds of miles apart. Genes show that the clams descend from two spring fields on opposite sides of the carcass, and within two years the bones were bare, while young of the same clams turned up at a third field.
P14.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P15.passage: A two-lane road laid across a valley floor in 1960 carried loaded logging trucks for thirty years, and surveyors checked it each fall against stakes along its shoulders. In 1983 an earthquake on a fault crossing the valley shifted the land north of it six feet east, and the road's yellow center stripe, once straight, now steps sideways at the fault, the asphalt there broken across both lanes. Stakes on either side showed the roadbed at the height it was laid, and trucks braking at the stop sign below the climb or crawling up it left the asphalt level. By 1990, its surface had been ______.
P15.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P16.passage: Every spring until 1914, the people of one moorland village set out together at dawn, crossed six miles of open common to its far edge, and came home by dusk. At the boundary stone they knelt in their best clothes by a spring that a parish legend said had cured a blind shepherd, drank from it in turn, and tied strips of cloth to the thorn above it. Folklorists who recorded the walk in 1900 called it the village's yearly ______. They walked home in silence between the grazing ponies, and the neighboring parish made the same walk to the same spring a week later.
P16.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P17.passage: Beside a rail line, a strip of uncut grass a few yards wide runs twelve miles across plowed farmland between two forests, and meadow voles live in both forests. Two decades of trapping suggest that the strip has served as the voles' ______. Voles born in the strip spend their lives in it: of thousands marked there, none has been trapped more than half a mile from where it was first caught, and forest voles seldom enter it. Strip voles live as long as forest voles, and each stretch of the strip now carries its own variants of a gene, unlike stretches a few miles away.
P17.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P18.passage: In 1590 a printer issued an engraved chart of a stretch of coast, copied from a navy surveyor's hand-drawn map. North is at the top of both, every cape, bay, and shoal sits where the survey puts it, and the print's open sea is as bare of ornament as the surveyor left it. The print fills a sheet twice as wide and twice as tall as the survey, so a harbor drawn an inch across in ink is two inches across in print. Its scale bar, too, is twice as long. Setting the two side by side, a historian found that the engraver had ______ the survey.
P18.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P19.passage: A glacier fills the head of a high valley whose river runs past farming villages to the plain. Seen from the plain thirty miles off, its white tongue points at the one notch where a road crosses the ridge, and old guidebooks tell drovers to walk toward it. Most of its meltwater sinks into deep gravel, so the river past the villages hardly changes between morning and night and in dry summers runs as low as the plain's rain-fed streams. Its front has held one rock ledge since the 1700s, through warm decades and cold. A study of three centuries of village records describes the glacier as the valley's ______.
P19.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P20.passage: In 1859 a merchant built a log store at a mountain gold camp, the only building there with a stove, an iron safe and a shelf of bottles, and his ledger survives. Through the long winters, miners whose cabins had no stove spent their evenings there, reading month-old newspapers aloud and playing cards at a table he kept by the fire, and the ledger shows them paying cash for a little tobacco and nothing more. One historian of the camp called the store, in those years, the camp's ______. The safe held his own takings, and the bottles held whiskey he would not sell after dark.
P20.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P21.passage: In 1790 a merchant ship carrying iron bars and casks of wine sank in thirty feet of water off a sandy coast that storms strike every winter. Two centuries on the seabed had ______ the ship, according to the divers who surveyed it in 1990. Within a few years of the wreck, a sandbar drifting along the coast came to rest over the spot where it sank. The divers located the hull only by probing with steel rods, and the deck they finally reached was smooth and pale, sound enough to hold a nail, with casks in the hold still full of wine.
P21.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P22.passage: In 1690 a merchant ship carrying iron bars and wine sank in sixty feet of water off a rocky coast. It came to rest on bare rock, and every winter's storms rolled it across the bottom until it broke apart. Divers in 1990 found its timbers hard and sound, worn round at the edges, strewn over a quarter mile, the iron bars piled in gullies and the wine jars in pieces among the boulders. The divers' report says that three centuries of seawater had ______ the ship. A section of keel lay two hundred yards from its stern post.
P22.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P23.passage: In 1890 a novel about a fishing family on a bleak northern coast, written in a small country's language, appeared in its first English translation. The translator kept the family's names, its fjord, its money and every chapter in order. Where the author wrote in short, broken sentences that repeat the same plain words, the translation runs in long, balanced periods, each repetition replaced by an apt variant. Every drowning and every winter of hunger is told in full. Set beside the original line by line, the translation shows that its translator ______ the novel. Reviewers praised its grace, a word no critic had used of the original.
P23.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P24.passage: In 1789 a fleet of eleven sailing ships left port carrying settlers along a coast of sandy bays and rocky headlands. In its third week at sea, the weather ______ several of the fleet's ships. A squall struck the fleet broadside in mid-channel, miles from any shore, and three ships, carrying full sail, heeled until the sea poured over their rails and did not come back up. Their crews were taken off the upturned hulls the next morning by ships that had ridden out the squall in plain sight of them a mile away.
P24.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P25.passage: For a decade the old salt mine served the nearby city's art museum as its ______. The mine's chambers lie six hundred feet down, where the air stays cool and dry all year, and a single lift shaft reaches them. After a flood soaked the museum, its water-stained paintings went down the shaft one batch at a time, and restorers worked on them in a lamp-lit chamber closed to the public. Each painting went back up within a year or two of arriving, its colors cleaned and its torn canvas patched.
P25.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P26.passage: A woolen mill stood on a hill trout stream from 1840 until 1930, and the next year a fisheries officer walked the stream from source to river. Its dam backed the stream into a pond half a mile long, where the surface barely carried a leaf, and the whole stream spilled over the wheel at the dam's foot and on downstream. Trout fed in the pond as they did in the stream above it, and cattle grazed down to the pond's reedy edges. His report judged that in ninety years the mill had ______ the stream.
P26.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P27.passage: In 1990 conservators began a ten-year survey of a ruined castle wall, half of which had been cloaked in ivy for two centuries. Where the ivy grew, its roots had followed the mortar joints deep into the wall. Stones there rocked at a touch, and a dozen lay in the grass at the wall's foot. Moisture readings in the stone behind the leaves matched those on the bare half, and stone faces under the stems were clean. The survey's final report says that the ivy had ______ the wall. On the bare half, stones set in the same mortar stood firm.
P27.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P28.passage: In 1960 a dam was built across a mountain river, holding back a reservoir three hundred feet deep. Twenty years of surveys show that the dam has ______ the river below it. A canal at the dam carries two thirds of the river to farms in the next valley, and the rest is released steadily, drawn from just beneath the reservoir's sunlit surface. Below the dam the river runs a third as wide each summer, and side channels where salmon spawned lie dry until fall; spring floods, too big for the canal, still pour over the spillway and scour the gravel bars. Bass still spawn just below the dam.
P28.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P29.passage: From 1952 to 1957 almost no rain fell on a pine forest in the southern hills, where foresters measured every tree yearly until 1975. Not one tree died during the drought, and through every dry summer the pines kept green needles. Once the rains returned, their growth rings stayed narrow for a decade, and in the 1960s bark beetles, which a healthy pine drowns in resin, killed one tree in five, large and small alike. The dead stayed standing for years until they rotted. The foresters' final report concluded that the dry years had ______ the forest.
P29.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P30.passage: One spring the river rose over its banks and stood on a farmer's lowest field for nine days. The field is a loose sand, and the water, clear from a reservoir upstream, kept sinking through it as fast as the river refilled it, and the sand was still dark and wet when the corn went in on schedule. It came up pale and short beside the dark green rows on the higher field. Walking the field in late summer, the county's soil scientist said that the flood had ______ it. Her samples showed less nitrogen in the topsoil than before the flood, and more in the farm's shallow well.
P30.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P31.passage: Two geologists measured the stones of a steep river running eight miles from granite and sandstone cliffs to the sea. Their report argued that the river had ______ those stones, and its photographs set out the case. Sieved, the bed held the same mix of sizes at the cliffs as at the sea. Painted stones moved a mile downstream with each flood, lying wherever they stopped. Below a spring seeping from the cliffs, every stone was orange outside but gray or red when cracked, and the spring's water leaves an orange film in a glass. Even at the sea, broken pebbles still fit back together edge to edge.
P31.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P32.passage: A city turned a forty-acre rail yard into a park, with a highway on its north edge and, to the south, row houses and apartment towers that the yard had divided for a century. Its lawns slope open to the highway, and its ball fields, playgrounds and weekend market sit in the middle. Gate counts found nearly all its visitors walking in from the row houses and towers in about equal numbers, on the same evenings, and staying two hours. A study of the park's first decade called it the district's ______. By decade's end a third of tower families counted row-house friends, up from one in twenty.
P32.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P33.passage: In 1902 a woman published the prairie diary her mother had kept from 1858 to 1871, and the mother's notebooks now sit in a state archive. Scholars who set the book beside the notebooks in 1990 found that the daughter had ______ the diary. Every sentence in the notebooks is in the book, and every sentence in the book is in the notebooks, in the same order. The mother's "chickins" and "sumer" are printed in standard spelling, and her long runs without a period are broken into sentences. The weekly egg tallies and the curses she wrote after quarrels with her husband appear in full.
P33.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P34.passage: A lone coral outcrop the size of a small car rises from the sand of a shallow lagoon, a quarter mile inside the reef that rings it. At dusk, parrotfish from the outer reef arrive one by one and wedge themselves into its crevices, each wrapping itself in a film of mucus that keeps off biting parasites, and lie still until dawn, when they swim back to graze the reef. Algae on the outcrop's flanks grows a foot long. Divers who have logged its visitors since 1985 call the outcrop the lagoon's ______.
P34.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P35.passage: On one island a thorny shrub with hollow thorns and nectar glands houses ants on nearly every plant. For three years an ecologist kept the ants off some shrubs with sticky bands and compared them with their neighbors. On the banded shrubs the flowers opened on schedule, stayed whole, and fell within days, while on their neighbors nearly every flower an ant had crawled through swelled into a pod. In those three years, the ants ______ the shrub. Caterpillars chewed both kinds of shrub alike, and banded shrubs grew just as tall; the pods split where they hung, dropping their seeds in a ring beneath the parent.
P35.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P36.passage: When wolves returned to a mountain valley in 1995, a pack of nine settled along the creek where a herd of four hundred elk spends each winter. Over the decade that followed, the pack ______ the herd. Collared wolves covered a mile or more at a run before nearly every kill, and the carcasses lay strung across the open benches above the creek, wherever an old cow or a calf had fallen behind. Between hunts the elk drifted back to the willow thickets along the creek, browsing them as low as ever, and the herd ranged over the whole valley floor.
P36.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P37.passage: For three summers an entomologist watched garden ants tend aphids on a row of beans, lapping up the honeydew the aphids release. Whenever a shoot began to wilt, workers carried its aphids in their jaws a few inches to the youngest leaves, where the aphids went on feeding. The aphids walked as quickly on leaves the workers had crossed as on clean ones, and their numbers rose all summer until the first frost killed them on the stems. Her report concludes that the ants had ______ the aphids. On a row the ants could not reach, aphids stayed on the wilting shoots and starved there.
P37.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P38.passage: In 1797 an occupying army entered a port city whose museum held some four hundred paintings and bronzes, many of them carried off from neighboring towns by the city's own fleet a century earlier. Soldiers cleared half the galleries in a single night, lifting canvases out of their frames and leaving the empty frames on the walls. Officers had marked beforehand each piece whose old label named a neighboring town, and the crates, each listed by number, sailed within the week to the towns on those labels, whose councils signed for them; this city's council was asked for no payment. Within a year, the army had ______ the museum's collection.
P38.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P39.passage: For thirty years beavers have lived on a creek in a dry mountain valley; the creek in the next valley has none. Their dams, a foot or two high, slow the creek without spreading it over the meadow, which lies under no standing water but stays soggy underfoot into autumn, and silt settling out of the still water raises the pond floors each year. The aspens on the slopes stand as thick as in the next valley. A hydrologist who has studied both valleys concludes that the beavers have ______ theirs. In dry summers the meadow along the creek stays green while the valley next door turns brown.
P39.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

P40.passage: From 1400 to 1700 a monastery stood on a ledge above the only road through a mountain valley, and its account books survive. Each year they record the duke's payment for keeping the valley's deeds and his treasury chests behind two iron doors in its cellar, which opened only on his written order. Clerks from the capital came to read the deeds in place, and none was ever copied. Its gate stayed locked; in plague years the valley's sick were turned away, and travelers on the road below bought their wine at the village inn. In those books, one historian has argued, the monastery appears as the valley's ______.
P40.question: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
